messages.subject: Re: 64-bit Windows
messages.body_plain:
A better solution is for the R community to get it's act together and make a 64 bit version of R for Windows 7 systems that simplifies the capability for porting a wonderful package like rattle.  If this is not done - and soon - R and Rattle will become irreverent.

The entire potential 64 bit R Community consists largely of people who are, or will be, working on Windows based systems.   They have been abandoned to small for profit companies who do not have the resources to do the ports and support them well.

If people on Windows systems are pushed into commercial packages, they will pick an established package that meets their price / support / functionality goals most closely.  I would hope otherwise, but it is probably not going to be Revolution R, ...

Regards, Richard Palmer

messages.subject: Re: 64-bit Windows
messages.body_plain:
Thanks  for the comments Richard.

I do note that R depends on the free contributions of others to make
things like this work.

I believe R 2.12.0 will run natively on MS/Windows 64 bit. If you
install the current development version of R 2.12.0 it does include a
64bit version. I have this running on Windows 7.

The problem (I am trying to solve at the moment) is that I can't find
a 64bit version of the Gtk+ libraries that I can install. That seems
to be an issue with the Gtk+ people rather than the R people (but then
I'm not quite sure). I presume the R people have figured out how to
compile R for MS/Windows 64bit using free software and perhaps that
knowledge could help compiling Gtk+ for 64 bit MS/Windows - perhaps
they are doing so and we will see it with the release of R 2.12.0.
Let's hope so.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject_clean: decision rules in one period to score on the later period in Ratttle
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rattle Users:

I used one dataset from a previous period to develop a predictive
model (classification tree) for diabetic members.  How do I use the
resulting decision rule to predict/score on a dataset from a later
period using Rattle?

I used the entrie dataset from period 1 to build the model and try to
score/classify on the dataset from period 2.  Does this have something
to do with portability?  Please advise.

The two datasets have exactly the same data elements/columns.

Thanks,

Albert

messages.subject: Rattle 2.5.42 Released
messages.body_plain:
A new release of Rattle is making its way to CRAN (currently on the
main server).

Check the Change Log link from
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rattle/index.html for details
of all changes since 2.5.31.

Main changes include:

Migration from using libglade to using GtkBuidler for the user
interface. libglade is deprecated and will not be avialable in R
2.12.0 on MS/Windows.

The rattle.info <http://rattle.info>() function has been extensively enhanced to list all
dependencies (packages) and their versions and any updates that are
available.

Many enhancements and bug fixes to modelling and scoring.

Regards,
Graham

Is it looking at one row (day) before or many rows (days) before when it makes the predictions? Since it is a prediction for the rain tomorrow it can’t be on the same row.

(And is the “RainTomorrow” data used as something to build the prediction for the next row on?)

What is the difference between classification and regression? Is it possible to see the difference in this example?

Kind regards

Rolf
